answer: Each of 447 aliases needs its own logbook histories, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. A amateur radio licence with callsign logbook history works as the gate: a callsign logged on the air for years. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The hollow record shows the asymmetry: scale multiplies the cost but never the reward, the bridge entry is checkable by anyone, and the reef window closes before a farm can catch up.
